# The two sides swapped, one line shorter: `account:` on
# `Assets:Suspense USD` and no `txn_split_guid:` at all.
#
# Naming only the transaction leaves the choice of split to the run, and what
# it picks is "the side that is not the `account:`" — here the **bank** split.
# One candidate, so nothing is ambiguous; 100.00 against 100.00 owed, so
# neither the fall-short nor the overpayment refusal has anything to say; and
# both sides being USD there is no conversion to refuse either.
#
# The sign guard is what catches the same mistake in the spelling that names
# the split, and it sits inside the restatement so that no caller can reach
# that without it. This spelling does not reach the restatement at all where
# the currencies agree — it takes the plain attach instead, which moved the
# +100.00 bank split onto the receivable with no sign asked.
#
# The deposit left `Assets:Bank:USD` entirely, the lot held the posting's
# +100.00 and this +100.00 so the invoice read as owing 200.00, and the entry
# still balanced, at exit 0.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal, with the bank's deposit still on the
# bank.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-02
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Suspense USD"
    txn_guid: "abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789"
